# Independent finite input-harness declaration review: v9

Reviewed frozen core patch `../input-harness-patch-v9.patch` SHA-256 `e70227f940ade60cd75a0769a5d75e68582e0a1fa12828b55a255da65a4f9a9a` and manifest `../manifest-v9.json` `bafbce9486ccc1a41baaa162b05d82a7c3b521a33813df91be6883fa60677f41`, against clean canonical `747e86a3e111292659963bed764605f0e1df5302`. Core patch apply check passes. This supersedes the v8 path-binding qualification only; v2–v6 hold records remain historical. The separate CI wiring patch was not reviewed or approved here.

V9 addresses v8's content-multiset limitation: each program source is realpath-resolved, located beneath its nearest package root, read as raw bytes and checked against compiler text; each record binds package name/version, package.json hash, normalized relative path, byte length and SHA-256. Duplicate package/version/path keys reject. The sorted JSON mapping is hashed and source count must be 70. Independently recomputed fingerprint `63959e2f4f016c60a1e13cf52a52fe53bee436f1b84ec786774faeb2ba05fbe7` from retained proof entries: 70 records for TypeScript 6.0.3, Material and CDK 22.1.7, and the candidate package. Included path-swap, duplicate and missing-record controls exercise the fingerprint function; transformed peer files/candidate declarations reject at the raw-byte or fixed-image boundary. These are finite drift controls, not independent proofs of general semantic equivalence. Exact byte/version policy makes later changes fail closed and require evidence-based requalification.

Independently copied the retained CI run manifest and exact tar to this directory and ran the patched script with `--run`: strict NodeNext packed consumer and all included drift/mutation controls pass, exit 0. Manifest SHA-256 `162230acd0beb6a6cc25e17a68f9dcdea6857f1f015ebe14118a16b15f5593a9` and tar SHA-256 `4a34df4d024f923dd8e701b9f1ed3b63f8f23fe2dc035cc6b5a1793e0cbf9a0e` match the retained originals. A copied manifest with library SHA changed to zeros is rejected with exit 1 before extraction. This uses retained files under a quiescent-workspace assumption, not a transaction against a privileged concurrent writer. The packed artifact is from `8a0c4866dba602bd1f9c9916128f7537d986e0b9`, not a new pack of canonical HEAD.

Independent row-array comparison confirms 52→39 open rows, exactly the 13 input-harness entries changed to recorded differences, no other row changes. Material/CDK 22.1.7 are declared minimum peers; v8 review independently checked the reference tag, actual tar declaration, public package resolution and static consumer scope. Transitive underscored declaration chunks are provenance reached through public exports, not authored private API imports, although the finite checker intentionally depends on their current paths and bytes. The qualification covers only these declaration rows and the tested minimum peer; it does not settle menu, DI, product behavior, or a broader peer range. Earlier 19 runtime cases used a different synthetic tar and do not establish full CI-artifact runtime behavior. No release or full gate claim, canonical writes, push or Actions.
